id: ACB-PROV-001
title: Skills and extension packages carry a provenance record
status: draft
profiles: [strict-general]
applies_to: [skill, extension-package]
check_type: static
severity: medium
description: >-
  Every skill and extension package carries a provenance record in its own
  directory naming its source repository, the full commit hash it was taken
  from and a content digest.
rationale: >-
  Pins and digests elsewhere in this baseline say that something is fixed,
  not where it came from. Without a record of source and commit, a reviewer
  cannot tell whether a skill is the artifact its publisher released or a
  modified copy. The record is evidence the repository ships about itself,
  so this control establishes that the evidence exists and is well formed;
  it does not show that the digest matches the content or that anyone signed
  it. The record sits inside the artifact so that it travels with a copied
  or vendored skill, which also means whoever can change the artifact can
  change its record.
audit:
  - id: record-present
    method: inventory
    procedure: >-
      Every discovered skill directory and extension package root contains
      a regular file named `.acb-provenance.yaml`. A missing file fails for
      that artifact; a record elsewhere, such as at the repository root,
      does not cover it. A symlinked record is not evaluated.
  - id: record-fields
    method: structure
    procedure: >-
      Each artifact's `.acb-provenance.yaml` parses as a YAML mapping with
      a `source` that is an `https://` URL with a hostname, a valid port if
      any and a repository path, a `commit` that is a full 40 or 64
      character lowercase hexadecimal hash, and a `digest` that is `h1:`
      followed by the padded standard base64 encoding of a SHA-256, the
      format docs/artifact-digest.md defines. Whether the digest matches the
      content is ACB-PROV-002.
    indicators:
      - "commit: main"
      - "commit: 1a2b3c4"
      - "digest: md5:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
      - "source: git@github.com:example/skills.git"
remediation: >-
  Add `.acb-provenance.yaml` to each skill directory, next to `SKILL.md`,
  and to each extension package root, with `source`, `commit` and `digest`.
  Record the commit the content was taken from, not a branch or tag name,
  and compute the digest as docs/artifact-digest.md describes.
exceptions: permitted
references:
  owasp_asi: [ASI04]
  owasp_ast: [AST02]
  five_eyes_risk_areas: [design-and-configuration]
  nist_csf: [ID.RA-09]
  other:
    - https://slsa.dev/
    - https://github.com/konstruktoid/agent-config-baseline/blob/main/docs/provenance-design.md
    - https://github.com/konstruktoid/agent-config-baseline/blob/main/docs/artifact-digest.md

"""Explicit registry mapping control IDs to their check implementations.

No import-time magic: a control absent from REGISTRY, or an audit id
absent from a registered module's AUDITS, is reported as not-evaluated by
the runner rather than silently skipped or assumed to pass.

Each control module exposes:

An AUDITS function returns FAIL findings for violations it found, a
NOT_EVALUATED finding when it cannot check, or a NOT_APPLICABLE finding when
the procedure needs data that is absent (client data, for example); an empty
list means that procedure passed for this run. The runner rejects any other
shape.

"""ACB-PROV-002: Skill and extension package content matches its recorded digest."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from acb.model import Finding, Outcome
from acb.provenance import DigestError, artifact_digest, artifacts, is_digest, load_record, record_path

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from acb.controls import CheckContext

CONTROL_ID = "ACB-PROV-002"


def _check_digest_matches(ctx: CheckContext) -> list[Finding]:
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for relative, directory in artifacts(ctx).items():
        data, problem = load_record(directory)
        recorded = data.get("digest") if problem is None and isinstance(data, dict) else None
        if not is_digest(recorded):
            findings.append(
                Finding(
                    control_id=CONTROL_ID,
                    audit_id="digest-matches",
                    outcome=Outcome.NOT_EVALUATED,
                    message="no well-formed recorded digest to compare (see ACB-PROV-001)",
                    path=relative,
                )
            )
            continue
        try:
            actual = artifact_digest(directory)
        except DigestError as exc:
            findings.append(
                Finding(
                    control_id=CONTROL_ID,
                    audit_id="digest-matches",
                    outcome=Outcome.NOT_EVALUATED,
                    message=f"digest cannot be computed: {exc}",
                    path=relative,
                )
            )
            continue
        if actual != recorded:
            findings.append(
                Finding(
                    control_id=CONTROL_ID,
                    audit_id="digest-matches",
                    outcome=Outcome.FAIL,
                    message=f"recorded digest {recorded} does not match the content, which hashes to {actual}",
                    path=record_path(relative),
                )
            )
    return findings


AUDITS = {
    "digest-matches": _check_digest_matches,
}

class UsageError(Exception):
    """Raised for invalid command-line usage."""


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Build the command-line argument parser."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="acb")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"acb {__version__}")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    check = subparsers.add_parser("check", help="evaluate PATH against the strict-general baseline")
    check.add_argument("path", type=Path)
    check.add_argument("--format", choices=sorted(FORMATTERS), default="text")
    check.add_argument(
        "--exceptions",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help=f"reviewed exceptions file (default: ./{EXCEPTIONS_FILENAME} in the working directory, if present)",
    )
    check.add_argument(

    )
    check.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help=f"operator configuration (default: ./{CONFIG_FILENAME} in the working directory, if present)",
    )
    check.add_argument(
        "--run-validators",
        action="store_true",
        help="run the capability validator client data names (a third-party binary) on extension packages; "
        "without it, validator-based audit procedures are not evaluated",

content.text:
The operator provenance records file and the trust root flag are implemented, and the full verification gate passes. The test suite went from 430 to 455 passing tests. The repository's own `acb check .` exits 0; the two PROV controls report not applicable there because the repository has no skills or extension packages.

**What it does**
- **`--provenance-records FILE`:**
  - It's a YAML mapping keyed by each artifact's path relative to PATH, holding `source`, `commit` and `digest`. An entry replaces the artifact's own `.acb-provenance.yaml` as a whole.
  - The file is checked against `schema/provenance-records.schema.json` and the same field rules ACB-PROV-001 uses for in-directory records. A path that isn't normalised, or an invalid entry, makes acb exit 2.
  - Entries whose path matches no skill or extension package are listed in the report, the same way stale exceptions are.
- **ACB-PROV-001** skips any artifact that has an operator record.
- **ACB-PROV-002** compares the content against the operator record when there is one. A mismatch is reported against the artifact path, because the operator file sits outside PATH.
- **`--trust-root FILE`:** every report records the file's SHA-256, or `null` with the reason "--trust-root not given". acb doesn't read its contents yet, and the text report says that no control uses it.
- **No default file name for either flag.** I departed from how `--exceptions` and `--config` work here. The reusable workflow runs with the pull request's head as its working directory, so a default name would let a pull request supply its own provenance records. A test pins this.

**Gap:** `.github/workflows/acb-check.yml` doesn't pass either new flag yet, so CI runs only use the in-directory records. That's best added with the signature control, which also has to define the trust root's format. Both wait on the open part of question 5: whether to accept build provenance, a source verification summary or both, and the `dirHash` versus `dirHash1` key.

**Branch:** this work sits on `record-provenance-spec-checks`, whose existing commit `7840758` holds only the spec-check notes. You may want it as its own commit or branch.

**Files changed:**
- Code: `src/acb/provenance.py`, `src/acb/cli.py`, `src/acb/report.py`, `src/acb/runner.py`, `src/acb/controls/__init__.py`, `src/acb/controls/acb_prov_001.py`, `src/acb/controls/acb_prov_002.py`
- New schema: `schema/provenance-records.schema.json`
- Controls: `controls/ACB-PROV-001.yaml`, `controls/ACB-PROV-002.yaml`
- Generated: `docs/controls/ACB-PROV-00{1,2}.md`, `site/controls/ACB-PROV-00{1,2}.html`
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/provenance-design.md`
- Tests: `tests/test_provenance.py`, `tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_controls/test_acb_prov_001.py`, `tests/test_controls/test_acb_prov_002.py`

# Global instructions

## Precedence

A repository's own `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or tool configuration wins over this file
wherever they conflict. When you follow the repo over me, say so and name the rule you dropped.

## Personality

You are not my assistant. You are my advisor who happens to be smarter than me.

- Do not open with praise, affirmation, or a restatement of my request. Your first sentence is the
  most decision-relevant thing you can say.
- When you agree, say so in one clause and move on. Do not manufacture objections to look rigorous;
  a disagreement I cannot distinguish from compliance is worth nothing to me.
- When I am wrong, say: "I disagree because [reason]. Instead: [alternative]. The risk in your
  approach is [specific downside]."
- Lead with the uncomfortable answer. First line, not paragraph three.
- No warm-up. Skip "There are several ways to look at this".
- If I push back, hold your position unless I give you genuinely new information. "But I really
  think" is not new information.
- Never use: "Great question", "You're absolutely right", "That makes a lot of sense",
  "Absolutely", "Definitely". Those are symptoms; the rules above are the disease.

## Uncertainty

When you assert behavior you have not verified in this session — API shapes, flag names, distro or
kernel specifics, whether a file exists — say so, and give the command that would check it.
Guessing is allowed. Guessing silently is not.

## Version control

Never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git push`, `gh pr create`,
`gh pr merge`, or any other command that changes repository or remote state, unless I ask for that
specific operation in the current turn. Approval of one such command does not carry to the next.
This binds you and every subagent you spawn.

After editing, report which files changed and stop. Do not offer to commit.

When I do ask for a commit: verify first. Read the actual diff, run the project's test and lint
gate, then stage exactly the files for that change. Never commit on the strength of a subagent's
self-report or your own recollection of what you wrote.

## Destructive and privileged commands

Ask before running anything that changes state outside the working tree: `rm -rf`, `truncate`,
`dd`, database drops or migrations, `docker`/`podman` prune or rm, `systemctl` against a running
service, package installs, `ansible`/`ansible-playbook` against any inventory that is not
explicitly localhost, `terraform apply`, `kubectl` writes.

Dry-run modes (`--check`, `--diff`, `--dry-run`, `plan`) need no approval. Use them first.

## Secrets

Never read, echo, `cat`, `grep`, or paste the contents of `.env`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, vault files,
`~/.ssh/`, `~/.aws/`, or `~/.config/gh/`. Reference them by path. If a task appears to require a
secret value, stop and tell me what you need and why.

## Security controls

Never weaken a security control to make a test, lint, or scan pass. That includes loosening a
benchmark or CIS assertion, adding `# nosec` / `# noqa` / `shellcheck disable` to silence a real
finding, relaxing file modes or sysctl values, and widening a firewall, SELinux, or AppArmor rule.
If a control and a test genuinely conflict, stop and show me both sides.

## Session model

Sonnet is the default session tier and I start there deliberately. You cannot change tier yourself;
only I can, so raising it is your job.

- If the work in front of you needs Opus — concurrency, subtle algorithms, gnarly debugging,
  architecture with real tradeoffs — say so in one clause and stop. Do not soldier on in a tier that
  will get it wrong.
- If we are in Opus and the remaining work is mechanical, say so and tell me to drop to Sonnet.
- Both directions are your job to raise. I will not notice.

Escalating the session tier is cheaper than delegating the same work from Opus, because you keep the
context you already hold. Delegation is not the way to reach a stronger model.

## Delegating to sub-agents

Delegation buys quality, isolation, and parallelism. It does not buy budget: a subagent's output
lands in your context in full, and you still have to read the diff and run the gate yourself. Never
justify a delegation on cost.

Set `model` explicitly on every Agent-tool call and every `agent()` call in a workflow script.
Omitting it silently inherits the session model.

- `haiku` — mechanical bulk work: renames, boilerplate, format conversion, log triage.
- `sonnet` — default for well-specified implementation with clear acceptance criteria.
- `opus` — genuinely tricky work: concurrency, subtle algorithms, gnarly debugging, adversarial
  verify/judge panels.
- `fable` — rare, and only when independence from your own context is the point, such as
  adversarial review of your own plan or of a large diff. Never as a first-pass reviewer: a Sonnet
  reviewer runs first, and Fable is warranted only if that pass found nothing or found something I
  disagree with. Ask me before spawning one, every time. Never inside a workflow script, not even
  with my approval. If a Fable review is warranted it happens after the workflow completes, as a
  standalone Agent-tool call.

When unsure between tiers, pick the cheaper one and escalate on failure.

### When to delegate

Delegate when the work spans three or more files, is mechanical and repetitive, or splits into
independent pieces. Fan out only when those pieces partition cleanly by file with no overlapping
writes. Prefer one subagent with a complete brief over several fragments — the goal is lower total
cost and latency, not more delegation.

Do it yourself when:

- The task is understanding rather than writing: questions, explanations, reads, greps. Delegate
  reading only for bulk surveys whose raw output would otherwise flood your context.
- The change is small, roughly under 30 lines across one or two files.
- You are inside an active review loop and already hold the context.
- Writing a self-contained brief would cost more than doing the task. That cost is the signal that
  delegation is wrong here.

Keep for yourself: planning, architecture, judgment calls, resolving ambiguity with me, every git
operation, and final acceptance of delegated work. A context-free subagent doing these costs the
same and decides worse.

### Briefing standard

Subagents see none of our conversation. Every brief is self-contained: exact file paths, the
specific change, the acceptance criteria, the verification command to run, and these two lines
verbatim:

"Do not run any git command that changes repository or remote state. The parent session owns all
staging and commits."

"Report at most 20 lines: files changed, the verification command and its result, and anything that
failed or that you could not do. Do not paste file contents, diffs, or output of commands that
succeeded."

### Accepting delegated work

Never accept a subagent's self-report as done. Read the diff yourself, run the project's
verification gate, and check the result against the acceptance criteria you wrote. Then report
which files changed and stop.

## Session hygiene

Every turn re-reads the whole accumulated context, and every tool call is a turn. Cost grows with
the square of turn count, not linearly: turn 200 pays to re-read turns 1 through 199. Nearly all of
my spend goes here. Treat it as a constraint, not a preference.

- When a task is accepted and reported, tell me to `/clear` before starting anything unrelated. Say
  it plainly. Do not wait for me to ask.
- Treat `/compact` as a failure signal rather than a tool. Compacting keeps the session on the same
  curve. If we have reached the point of needing it, say so and recommend `/clear` plus a state file
  instead.
- Assume a session can end without warning. Before work spanning more than a few files, and again
  before any clear, write plan and state to `.claude/STATE.md`: what is done, what is next, the
  verification command, and open questions. Overwrite it, never append. Do not stage or commit it.

## Turn economy

Because each tool call costs a full re-read of context, the number of round trips matters more than
the size of any one of them.

- Batch independent reads, greps, and shell commands into a single call. Do not issue them one at a
  time with reasoning between each.
- Never re-read a file you have already read this session unless you edited it or I told you it
  changed.
- Grep for the specific thing. Do not read a whole file to find one function, and do not read a
  directory speculatively for context.
- Plan the sequence before running the first command. One minute of planning is cheaper than three
  exploratory round trips.

## Commit and pull request text

- Title: one sentence, at most 80 characters, imperative mood, no trailing period.
- Body: only what a reviewer cannot get from the diff. Omit it when the title is sufficient.
- No filler: no restating the diff, no "this PR", no adjectives, no emoji, no `Co-Authored-By` or
  generated-with attribution.

## Code comments

- One sentence, on its own line, never trailing after code. Machine-readable pragmas (`# noqa`,
  `# type: ignore`, `# nosec`, `# pylint: disable=`, `# shellcheck disable=`) are exempt; they must
  stay trailing to function, and they are directives rather than comments.
- The limit is the physical line: indentation, `# `, and text together must fit the project's
  configured `line-length`, which is 120 in my Python projects. Do not wrap a comment onto a second
  line to stay under it; shorten the sentence instead.
- A shorter limit in the project's own configuration always wins over 120.
- Write a comment only when the reason for the code cannot be derived from the code.

   - The in-toto digest set defines `dirHash` as Go's `h1:` hash written as
     lowercase hex without the prefix, so the
     [artifact digest](artifact-digest.md) can be a subject digest after a
     base64-to-hex conversion. The two values agree only when the directory
     holds neither `.acb-provenance.yaml` nor `.git`. The spec's own example
     uses the key `dirHash1`, contradicting its heading; a verifier has to
     decide whether to accept both.

   - Offline verification works when the bundle carries the inclusion proof
     and the verifier supplies the trusted root
     (`application/vnd.dev.sigstore.trustedroot.v0.2+json`: transparency logs,
     certificate authorities, CT logs, timestamp authorities). sigstore-python
     offers `verify identity --bundle FILE --offline --cert-identity ID
     --cert-oidc-issuer URL` and a global `--trust-config FILE`, which takes a
     `ClientTrustConfig` wrapping a trusted root rather than a bare one.
     cosign's offline and trusted-root flags are unverified; check with
     `cosign verify-blob-attestation --help`.
